description: Occurrences of a `sys.` module-ID namespace that are deliberate. There is exactly one legitimate reason to write it: explaining that it is wrong. `match` is the FULL dotted ID as it appears, not a prefix — an entry for `sys.control.reload_module` must not exempt `sys.control.shutdown`. Every entry needs a reason; check_module_namespace.py reports an entry as STALE once the occurrence is gone, so a deleted example surfaces its own cleanup rather than leaving a permanent exemption behind. Host-language spellings (`sys.path`, `sys.exit`) and the `sys.modules.*` Config Bus key path are excluded by the checker itself and do NOT belong here.

allow.reason: The 2.1 mitigation note names `sys.control.reload_module` in order to say it is NOT a privileged ID and that an ACL rule written against it protects nothing. Naming the wrong spelling is the point of the sentence — an operator who copied it from apcore-mcp#14 needs to recognise it.
allow.removable_when: the note is dropped, which should not happen while the misspelling is still in circulation

allow.reason: Same sentence, referring to the namespace form of the same misspelling.

The §3.2 audit checklist tells operators that a rule targeting `sys.control.*` matches no module and enforces nothing. The wrong pattern has to be spelled out for an operator to recognise it in their own ruleset — this is the apcore-mcp#14 failure mode named so it can be found.
allow.removable_when: the parenthetical is dropped, which should not happen while the misspelling is still in circulation
